data.name: BlazBlue: Continuum Shift Extend
data.detailed_description:
Oferta especial

  • PC version includes the system voice feature for 7 characters which was sold separately for the console version.

  • Bonus content includes Special Original Soundtrack and BlazBlue Art Collection.
    The bonus contents will be placed in your Steam folder: ..\Steam\SteamApps\common\BlazBlue Continuum Shift Extend\Digital Extras[/list]


    Acerca do jogo

    The second entry in the critically acclaimed BlazBlue franchise, BlazBlue: Continuum Shift Extend adds a number of game play modes, story scenarios, new moves, and an all-new playable character to further enhance the BlazBlue experience and solidify its status as one of the all-time great 2D fighters.

    Story
    Several years after the end of the Second War, multiple branches of the Librarium reputed to command a force as powerful as an entire nation’s army were suddenly and utterly destroyed. Inexplicably, the hidden cauldrons within each branch were also completely decimated. The few survivors spoke in hushed, shaken tones of a single man who had
    appeared out of nowhere, cutting down all in his path.

    Main Game Features
    • Expanded Character Roster: In addition to the downloadable characters offered for the previous entry in the series (Makoto, Valkenhyn, and Platinum the Trinity), EXTEND introduces Relius Clover, the mad puppeteer and Carl's father, as a playable character. Master a whole new way of fighting with Relius as he uses his marionette, Ignis, to turn the tide of battle.
    • Enhanced Story Mode: Relive and rediscover the events that took place in BlazBlue: Calamity Trigger or venture forth into one of four all new story scenarios!
    • New and Revised Game Modes: Take on the strongest of foes in Unlimited Mars Mode or fight your way to the bottom of Abyss Mode!
    • Fully Revised Combat System: All characters, new and old, have been thoroughly rebalanced and armed with all new strategies and combos to take your game to the top!

reviews.review:
(This review contains no meaningful information about the game. It's just the writer's ramblings. Check other reviews for important content)

[h1]So, you're already a BlazBlue fan?[/h1]

Hey you, yes you, the one checking out reviews for BlazBlue Continuum Shift. If you were new to the series, you'd probably look at reviews for either the first game (in order to start the story from the beginning) or the last game (in order to get straight to the multiplayer), so if you're here at the second game, you must already be familiar with BlazBlue and just curious what other people had to say.

Well, that or you got brought here by the Steam Discovery Queue or something and don't even know what this game is (In which case, you might want to go to [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/263300/BlazBlue_Calamity_Trigger/]Calamity Trigger[/url] for the first game or [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/586140/BlazBlue_Centralfiction/]Centralfiction[/url] for the last), but I'm going to write under the assumption that you already know BlazBlue because it gives me a flimsy excuse to treat the whole review as meaningless anyway because no one starts a series like this at entry number 2, and so instead I'll just talk about stuff no one else on the planet cares about but me, so let's get to it.

[h1]Spoilers ahead (for the entire series, I mean, not just Continuum Shift)[/h1]

So yeah, I went through, Calamity Trigger, I went through Continuum Shift, I went through, Chronophantasma, I went through Centralfiction, I 100%-ed the story mode in each, I finished every arcade story (even in Centralfiction which for [i]some[/i] reason gave most characters 3 different arcade stories, and it's not like it's tedious or anything running through this [b]97 times[/b]), I watched all the Teach Me Miss Litchis, and after all that, I'm pleased to say that I [i]still[/i] don't know what's happening in this series.

[b]Things that exist based on loops:[/b]

First off, how do time loops work? Because I'm not entirely sure, and I can see two different ways this could go down, neither of which quite makes sense.

The first possibility is that Jin falls in a cauldron or something and time travels to the past to become Hakumen. This is purely "ordinary" time travel and is unrelated to the entire world being in 100 year loops. If this is the case, then I don't understand where Hakumen came from in the timeline where we manage to break the loops because I don't think Jin ever went to the past there.

The second possibility is that Jin falls in a cauldron or something and floats around in the Boundary. Meanwhile, Ragna and Nu merge into a Black Beast and the Master Unit resets the world because of it. Since Jin was in the Boundary and this is outside of reset territory (I think? I know Kokonoe mentioned keeping data backups in the Boundary at one point which were unaffected by reality warping shenanigans, so I think this is the case. Honestly, though, isn't Arakune's soul in the Boundary? Does this imply there are hundreds of Arakunes running around in there from various time loops?), he's free to fall into the next loop to become Hakumen there. If this is the case, I don't understand how the very first time loop got its Hakumen as there couldn't have been a previous loop to snatch a Jin from. Or did it just not and the first time around we only had 5 Heroes?

[b]Rachel intervening:[/b]

Rachel is not supposed to get involved with what happens in the world but she's just supposed to observe it, and yet, she seems to intervene, like, all the time constantly without repercussions. Like she's the one who made Jin into Hakumen, right? Potentially hundreds of times in all the various loops (Though I don't know if having her powers drained persists between loops or not, and maybe if she didn't interfere with [i]this[/i] version of the world, it doesn't count anymore, though I'm purely just making that up and don't think I've ever heard it said either way how it works), and, you know, is creating a hero needed to save the entire world not a pretty big intervention? Why is that allowed? Unless of course we're sticking with the 5 Heroes theory, in which case I would find it amusing that Hakumen is redundant and creating him doesn't even count as important because he's secretly a loser and Rachel just likes letting Jin play hero to mess with his head for giggles, but something tells me that's not the intended canon reason behind this, so what exactly counts as interference here?

[b]Did events happen one time or many?[/b]

Somewhat related to the above, but Clavis Alucard apparently dies in the year 2107. This is after the start of the time loops, so does Rachel watch her dad die many times? But didn't she inherit the role of observer for the world after he died? So how does that work? Is she continually regaining this role and every time he dies a bunch of memories come flooding back into her or something from other loops? But I'm not entirely convinced that's the case because in Calamity Trigger during one of Jin's endings we see an illustration that I assume is Rachel about to give Jin the Hakumen armor because I'm pretty sure she says something like "[noparse]Mr. Hero[ of Ikaruga], how would you like to become a real Hero[ of the 5 Heroes plus Hakumen the loser]?[/noparse]" And in that picture she seems to be her usual age, whereas other times when we see Rachel with Clavis she appears noticeably younger, and so I would assume she is somehow made completely ageless between loops and just retains whatever age she had when she became an observer or something, so... Is there a second Rachel running around who secretly spies on her younger self? But then where does her younger self go later? Did Clavis die once in some sort of "original" timeline and in loops after that he just stays dead? I don't know what's going on here, man, I really don't.

And honestly, it's not even like I think this series is full of plot holes or anything, but I can only assume [i]something[/i] must explain all this, that there must be some line of dialogue that I failed to recognize the significance of, some clue that I missed, [i]something[/i] that means all of this adds up, but I just honestly have no idea what it even might remotely be, and I'm just left feeling like I'm only looking at half of the puzzle.
